criterion_units.evidence: To select B and reject the distractors, the student must interpret speed from velocity in a motion context (Unit 4), differentiate v(t)=te^{-t} using the product rule and derivative of e^u with chain rule (Units 2 and 3), and use the sign change of v'(t)=e^{-t}(1-t) to identify the time of the maximum speed rather than an endpoint or no maximum (Unit 5).

To determine the time at which speed is greatest, a student must first understand that speed is the magnitude of velocity (Unit 4.2). Since v(t) = t*e^(-t) is non-negative for t>=0, speed = v(t). The first derivative test (Unit 5.4) or analysis of function behavior, including limits at infinity (Unit 1.15), is then used to confirm the maximum value.
